chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Hillyard on the St. Louis boat; Ben Sparks
summary: Whether Hillyard was on the boat; his thin look; the large Ben Sparks and his remark about a strong wind.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: SOME OF THE GUYS WERE NOT TOO CRAZY ABOUT HIM. THE GUYS AROUND ST. LOUIS WERE NOT ALL THAT CRAZY ABOUT HIM. WELL APPARENTLY HE DIDN'T LEAVE JEETER'S BAND UNDER THE MOST FAVORABLE CONDITIONS, YOU KNOW LIKE HE SLIPPED OUT, HE WAS AN AGITATING KIND OF GUY, WELL IT DOESN'T CONCERN US ANY WAY (inaudible) HE WAS REHEARSING WITH BILLY JACKSON'S BAND WHEN HE WAS STILL SUPPOSED TO BE WORKING WITH PHILLIPS WAS HILLYARD ON THE BOAT FROM ST. LOUIS.
I THINK IT WAS CHESTER CLARK WHO PLAYED WITH YOU AND THE LEAD HAVE BEEN JEETER AND MAYBE HILLYARD. HOLLOWAY WASN'T IN THE BAND STILL AND HAYMEN WASN'T IN THE BAND. SO IT HAS TO BE HILLYARD.
I think Hillyard was on that boat.
HILLYARD WOULD HAVE BEEN A YOUNG GUY TOO.
WELL HE WAS A GOOD MUSICIAN WASN'T HE?
HOW WAS HE? WAS HE HARD TO GET ALONG WITH?
No, everybody thought he had tuberculosis, he looked like he was (inaudible).

Funny thing about him Ben Sparks he was great big guy and he was always talking about one of these days a strong wind would blow him over and he would never get up any more. He outlived Benny many years.
